scope: One original minigame in one desktop browser using a privately prepared player-local module.

sections.title: Browser loop, guest contexts and time
Audible original audio and player input

priorities.title: Runtime and admission bottlenecks
priorities.reason: Execution boundaries and host-thread delivery constrain graphics, audio and input. Establish a viable target admission route and demonstrate continuing guest execution with preserved state and responsive browser delivery. Implement only the contexts/timers the target requires; keep later title audio/input timing checks explicit. A general Xbox scheduler is not an exit requirement.

priorities.title: Original graphics, including an early title frame
priorities.reason: This group has the broadest known feature list. After the minimum context/surface/submission path, test **MB15 shader/combiner translation early**, then cover the required textures, surfaces and state. Use existing translators and the backend seam. Attempt an original frame as soon as its required slices work; do not wait for a complete renderer or all menu features. Component proofs alone do not close title rendering.

priorities.title: Original audio
priorities.reason: Resolve format/mixer/streaming compatibility while there is still time to change the integration. Prove one required original sound through the chosen browser output, then the additional features required by the selected path. Pull forward its necessary file and timing dependencies.

priorities.title: Finish the selected startup and resource path
priorities.reason: Finish the resource/lifetime and continuation work needed for the chosen round. The subset needed for priorities 1–3 must already have been pulled forward. This position never means attempting title graphics/audio without their real resources; it defers unrelated startup families and unused loader features.

priorities.title: Original input and controllable menu
priorities.reason: Connect one chosen host method to original pad polling, verify press/release/focus behavior, and operate the original menu. Pull a minimal input connection forward if it is needed to reach an earlier proof. Full remapping and extra devices remain later-milestone scope.

priorities.title: Complete the original round/results/return
priorities.reason: This larger integration item needs the menu and shared systems first. Inventory its likely feature requirements in MB01; promote any newly observed large graphics/audio/runtime gap to its owning earlier priority instead of collecting it in a final cleanup batch. Exit with one complete original cycle.

priorities.title: Bounded corrections and M1 acceptance
priorities.reason: Complete the three consecutive audiovisual/input cycles and independent acceptance review. Required correctness checks accompany each earlier change; final acceptance is additional scenario evidence. Unrelated polish, all-game support and the broad device matrix do not enter this queue.

items.title: Freeze the M1 scenario
items.startingPoint: M1's three-cycle gate is defined; a specific game/input/browser execution recipe must be recorded. Select one compatible build, minigame, desktop browser/device and input/seat configuration.
items.completion: A repeatable original menu-to-results input recipe and required feature list exist. Choose the target from evidence; the prototype's game is not automatically the least costly original path.

items.title: Assess the reached 4EA30 caller
items.startingPoint: Reported local R3 returns through the logger and stops before this caller's body. Its name/behavior is not established by its address.
items.completion: Produce the retained byte/layout, caller/argument/resource/provider contract and direct-dependency list for this exact invocation. Mark any missing authority. This is a bounded assessment, not permission to admit the body.

items.title: Complete the selected startup continuation
items.startingPoint: Startup still has an active original enclosing function; existing C/SDK providers can be reused where their contracts apply.
items.completion: The assessed family returns to its actual original caller with required state preserved, or names the next unsupported family and its exact missing capability. Use MB02 first; assign child batches to this row instead of predicting a task per stop. Additional families before the menu remain conditional work.

items.title: Establish title-slice admission capacity
items.startingPoint: The accepted profile uses 511/512 function charges and 64/64 bindings. Whole-image generation is separate from browser admission.
items.completion: A target-path inventory and retention/dispatch comparison show a viable capacity route. First inspect duplicate/unused representations; any change to ceilings/module contracts needs its own scoped review. Question: what capacity does MB01's path actually demand? Do not silently raise limits.

items.title: Connect sustained execution to browser delivery
items.startingPoint: Worker startup works; no accepted playable execution/input/presentation loop exists. Select a safe stepping/yield or other reviewed delivery scheme instead of assuming the proof's one-shot run is sufficient.
items.completion: Guest execution continues while required input, frame and audio delivery remain responsive. Preserve actual guest context and unsupported stops. Question: which existing generated execution boundary can safely support the chosen scheme? Do not infer original timing from the accumulator's default 60 Hz.

items.title: Execute the required guest contexts/callbacks
items.startingPoint: Context creation, TLS/FS/frame components and selected immediate synchronization models exist; a READY context or admitted callback is not proof it ran.
items.completion: Each context/callback required by the scenario enters, returns or blocks/wakes with correct ownership and preserved state. Use only the scheduling behaviors actually required; prove the selected callback before building a general scheduler. Question: which callbacks/waits does MB01 exercise?

items.title: Deliver required clock/timer events consistently
items.startingPoint: Clock values, timer queues and DPC components are tested separately. Their existence does not connect elapsed browser time to original callback delivery.
items.completion: Guest-observed time, required timer/DPC delivery and input/audio ordering agree for the selected foreground scenario and defined stalls. Question: which clock consumers and timer events are actually required? Share one reviewed policy with MB05/06; broad device timing calibration belongs beyond this gate.

items.title: Bridge a selected local range into guest I/O
items.startingPoint: The selected File/Blob can be inspected and read in bounded ranges; the title's supported read interface is not connected to that reader.
items.completion: A source-supported original request reaches the local reader and exact bytes reach the checked guest destination. Define worker/synchronous delivery, ownership and error/cleanup behavior; review any new host capability explicitly. Question: which reached request supplies the first unambiguous path/range/buffer contract?

items.title: Complete the required guest file lifecycle
items.startingPoint: Namespace, handles, FATX and selected negative disc-open behavior exist. Successful disc opens, reads, positions/queries and closes remain caller-specific.
items.completion: The selected original open/read/query/close sequence returns actual bytes/status/IOSB and releases ownership without affecting unrelated files. Implement only the target's requested operations; reuse MB08 transport.

items.title: Load the selected game's required resources
items.startingPoint: Asset/package preview parsers and generated title code exist. Preview reads do not establish that the original loader can consume its resources.
items.completion: The original loader reaches its real continuation with the required on-device resources and lifetimes. Inventory its package/format needs and choose existing original/SDK providers. GPU texture/shader translation belongs to MB14/15 and audio decoding to MB18; do not count those implementations twice. Question: which extra non-GPU/non-audio provider gaps remain?

items.title: Select context ownership and wire the backend seam
items.startingPoint: WebGL2 context creation exists in the preview; the title GPU interface has no integrated browser backend.
items.completion: One selected backend/context instance is called through a checked resource boundary and can be torn down. Decide worker versus main-thread ownership and synchronous versus marshalled calls. Produce a precise interface/build spike; avoid building both architectures.

items.title: Render surfaces and present frames
items.startingPoint: A preview canvas exists; title render targets, depth surfaces and presentation ownership are unconnected.
items.completion: The selected surface/target allocation, lifetime and final presentation path produces a frame on the intended canvas with correct dimensions. Reuse MB11 ownership; MB16 owns clear/viewport/state ordering. Question: which target/surface formats and transitions does the first original frame need?

items.title: Submit vertices, indices and primitives
items.startingPoint: One checked raw-FVF triangle and geometry prepasses have component evidence. Full original submissions do not.
items.completion: The target's required vertex/index layouts, spans and primitive paths produce independently checked buffers/draws; unsupported layouts stop before unsafe access. Start from the first observed submission, then list additional required layouts.

items.title: Upload textures and apply sampler state
items.startingPoint: Host texture preparation and preview uploads exist; guest resource descriptors, levels/stride and title sampler transitions are not bound to the backend.
items.completion: The selected title texture formats/levels upload and sample correctly through checked ownership, with unsupported formats refused. Question: which actual format/stride/filter/addressing combinations does MB01 require?

items.title: Translate required shader/combiner programs
items.startingPoint: Native SDK/OpenCE translation components are reuse candidates; the preview shader is independently authored.
items.completion: Required original vertex-program/pixel-combiner paths execute through the selected backend with a checked reference comparison. Inventory actual instructions, constants and combiners, including skinning inputs only if the target uses them, then split feature families. Question: which title programs/features can existing translators cover?

items.title: Apply observed draw-state sequences
items.startingPoint: Preview depth/blend toggles and bounded device/FIFO components exist. They do not implement original state or hardware readiness.
items.completion: The target's observed viewport, clear, depth/stencil/blend/cull and draw ordering produce the expected sequence. Add a fence/synchronization feature only when the selected call path requires it. Use source/reference semantics, not synthetic read-back as GPU-ready evidence. Keep texture/shader implementation in MB14/15; this row owns state ordering.

items.title: Join the backend to an actual original frame
items.startingPoint: Graphics component proofs and original startup are currently separate.
items.completion: The locally selected original module reaches the implemented GPU path and presents an original frame with identified resources/state and a controlled comparison. Reuse only the MB11–16 feature slices required by the observed path; this row owns the title hookup and evidence, not another renderer. It requires the relevant startup/resource path, whose exact order must come from observation.

items.title: Supply the required original sound-buffer/voice behavior
items.startingPoint: A narrow preview decoder exists; original sound resource/API/buffer/voice processing is not integrated.
items.completion: A selected original sound request produces the correct bounded PCM/buffer state, with required start/stop/loop/voice behavior. Reuse native/SDL components where compatible. Question: which formats, mixer features and streaming behaviors are actually used by the target? Add only that subset first.

items.title: Deliver audible browser output
items.startingPoint: Preview WebAudio and a silent SDL callback are separate host proofs.
items.completion: MB18's original sound reaches the chosen browser output after permitted user activation, with sample/clock/lifecycle evidence and audible output. Measure underruns and teardown; use MB05/07's scheduling policy. Select one output route rather than requiring both WebAudio and SDL implementations.

items.title: Connect one host input method to original pad polling
items.startingPoint: Keyboard/gamepad prototype adapters and Xbox packet/device components exist, but no accepted original input-driven round exists.
items.completion: The chosen keyboard-to-virtual-pad or physical-gamepad path changes the original guest controller packet and the title consumes it. Match packet/device/mapping contracts to retained evidence. M1 does not require every input device; keyboard input does not imply adding an original Xbox keyboard device.

items.title: Deliver fresh input and clear stale actions
items.startingPoint: Prototype focus/disconnect clearing exists; the original worker/poll path is not connected.
items.completion: Press/release and focus loss reach the selected guest controller without stale or reordered actions. If the chosen path uses Gamepad API, verify its main-thread/proxy requirement. Use MB05/07 and the selected input method; full remapping/all-device acceptance belongs to later milestones.

items.title: Operate the original menu
items.startingPoint: No controllable original screen is accepted. The host, renderer and input pieces still need to meet in the title.
items.completion: Original menu output responds to recorded input and selects the target route. Compose MB03/05, required resources, MB17 and MB20/21; identify any newly reached capability against its owning row.

items.title: Complete the selected original round and return
items.startingPoint: The original game/round/results join is not observed. Its rules should execute through retained original code.
items.completion: The selected original round reaches results and returns to the original menu, with required audio and input. Reuse shared paths; add only the newly observed target-specific feature gaps. No approximate rules or replacement scenes. Question: what does this path exercise beyond the menu?

items.title: Accept three complete cycles
items.startingPoint: The M1 criterion and report/audit infrastructure exist; its full scenario has not passed.
items.completion: Three consecutive original menu/game/results/menu cycles pass with visible output, audible audio, recorded input, source/module/device identities, control comparison and independent acceptance review. Targeted component results feed the gate; task closure alone cannot accept it.
